environment.scope: whole process and inherited fresh children; selected ancestor attribution is sampled CPU, not phase latency

lexical_vs_name_interpretation.lexical_text_resolution: no standalone clone_bounded_text frame in no-inline output; this is unresolved/inlined, not evidence of zero cost
lexical_vs_name_interpretation.shared_allocator_leafs: malloc, memmove, and deallocation symbols are shared across parser, expanded Name, event, frame, and verification paths and are not uniquely assigned to lexical copies

limitations: Perf data includes process startup, per-child corpus reconstruction, archive verification, and post-operation semantic verification; those are excluded only by the selected-cell ancestor stack filter, not by a separate timestamp boundary in perf.
The selected-cell operation scans the source worksheet stream to EOF; the selected ancestor subset therefore includes the selected stream parser and its MCE/x14ac callbacks.
The capture used a clean detached worktree at the candidate revision; route and MCE source bindings hash Git blobs from that exact revision.
A single current-state capture supports hotspot evidence only. It does not support an optimization speedup, regression, or ABBA claim.
purpose: Current-state descriptive CPU attribution for xlsx_file_selected_cell; no before/after or speedup claim
recommendation: Residual expanded-name allocation remains a measured hotspot after attribute-name reuse. Element/frame and raw-observer ownership still require copies under the current public API. Use the dynamic target_metrics table and direct-caller attribution for follow-up selection; this single profile does not establish a paired CPU speedup or a broad lexical-copy bottleneck.
